pages.title: Run a refinance
pages.description: Open a loan’s refinance, check where today’s loan stands, and read the verdict: can you refinance, and should you?
pages.intro: The refinance answers two questions about a loan: can the property support a new loan the size of what you owe, and is it worth doing? It is worked out live from the property’s T12 (or its approved underwriting) and today’s rates. Nothing about the loan changes until you save something.
before: The property’s T12, uploaded in Underwriting — see [Upload a T12](upload-a-t12). A refinance is never sized on a typed NOI.

steps.text: Open the loan’s page: click its property on the **Portfolio** tab, or pick it under **Specific Property**. See [Open a loan](open-a-loan).
Click **Refi Calculator** at the top of the loan’s page. The refinance opens in its place.

marks.label: Refi Calculator
marks.text: Opens the refinance for the loan on this page.

steps.text: Read **Current Loan**: what you owe, the rate, the monthly payment and when the loan matures. A hybrid loan also says when its rate resets and what the payment becomes.

marks.label: Current Loan
marks.text: Today’s loan, from its record.

marks.label: Rate reset
marks.text: Here the rate resets within a month, and the payment jumps.

marks.label: What kind of deal?
marks.text: A new loan, or an extension with today’s lender.

steps.text: Leave **What kind of deal?** on **New loan**. To keep today’s lender on new terms instead, see [Extend with today’s lender](extend-with-your-lender).

callouts.text: A property with no T12 shows **No T12 yet** instead of a verdict, with a button that opens Underwriting on it.

steps.text: Scroll to **Coverage & value** and check the **NOI basis**: the NOI the whole refinance is sized on. It is **In-place T12** until the property’s underwriting is approved; then you can pick **Safe underwriting** or **Aggressive underwriting**.

marks.label: NOI basis
marks.text: In-place T12 here. Safe and Aggressive are greyed until the underwriting is approved.

marks.label: DSCR today
marks.text: The NOI ÷ a year of today’s payments.

marks.label: Coverage today
marks.text: Whether today’s coverage clears your DSCR floor.

steps.text: Under **Exit cost (prepay penalty)**, pick the penalty type from the loan documents. Until you do, the cost is marked **assumed** and estimated as yield maintenance.

callouts.text: These figures are screening estimates. Confirm them with the loan documents and a rate sheet before you act.

steps.text: Scroll to the colored box under **What to push**. Its first line is the answer; the line at the bottom says what to do.

marks.label: The answer
marks.text: Here: act before the rate resets, and pay down the gap.

marks.label: You owe (payoff)
marks.text: What a new loan has to pay off.

marks.label: Property supports
marks.text: The biggest loan the property supports at the proposed rate and the lender’s limits.

marks.label: Can you?
marks.text: Whether that covers what you owe, and which limit caps it.

marks.label: Bottom line
marks.text: What to do, in one line.

steps.text: Read **Can you?**. When the answer is yes, **Should you?** under it says whether it is worth doing: the interest the new rate saves, against the early-payoff penalty.

callouts.text: The answer is one of four: **Refinance**; **Your decision**, when only the cash out makes it worth it; **Don’t refinance**; or **Act before** a date **— pay down** an amount, when the rate resets or the loan ends within 12 months and the property can’t support what you owe. See [The verdict](ref-refinance#the-verdict).

steps.text: To refinance, type your lender’s quote and check the proposed loan. See [Set the proposed loan’s rate and amount](set-the-proposed-loan).
Click **Save as a loan** at the top to make the proposed loan a loan. See [Save the refinance as a loan](save-the-refinance).
Or click **Close** to go back to the loan’s page.

callouts.text: Closing loses nothing. The lender’s limits, an appraisal and the kind of deal you picked are kept with the property for the whole team.

next.text: Type your lender’s quote and its limits.
See what pushing the NOI would get you.
Every figure and control on the refinance, named.

pages.title: Set the proposed loan’s rate and amount
pages.description: Type your lender’s quote, test a smaller loan, set the lender’s limits and check the new loan’s terms.
pages.intro: The proposed loan starts from today’s loan’s rate type, a usual spread, and the biggest amount the property supports at the usual limits. Put in your lender’s own quote and limits to see the verdict for the loan you can really get.
before: Your lender’s quote: the rate type, the index and the spread, and the limits it sizes a loan on.

steps.text: Open the loan’s refinance and scroll to **Proposed rate**, inside the colored verdict box. See [Run a refinance](run-a-refinance).
Click the rate type your lender quotes: **Fixed**, **Floating** or **Hybrid**.

marks.label: Rate type
marks.text: It starts as today’s loan’s type: here Hybrid, fixed for the first years.

marks.label: Index
marks.text: What the rate is priced on.

marks.label: Spread (bps)
marks.text: The lender’s quote over the index.

marks.label: Rate
marks.text: The index today + the spread.

steps.text: Pick the **Index** your lender prices on, and type its quote in **Spread (bps)** (100 bps = 1%). For **Hybrid**, set the index and the margin for the years after the fixed period too. The verdict and the proposed loan update at once.
For **Floating**, also fill in **Rate floor (%)**, **Rate cap (%)** and **Cap cost (bps/yr)** if your lender asks for them.

callouts.text: A yellow **starting spread** tag means the spread is still the app’s starting figure, taken from your recent loans of this kind. It goes once you type the lender’s quote.

steps.text: Type an amount in **Proposed loan amount**. It starts at what the property supports; a smaller loan means more cash to pay in. The line under it shows that loan’s coverage, LTV and debt yield.

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: Here a made-up $25,000,000.

marks.label: At this amount
marks.text: Its coverage (amortizing and interest-only), LTV and debt yield.

sections.title: Set the lender’s limits
sections.text: The property supports the smallest loan that your lender’s limits allow. They start at 1.25× / 75% / 7%, all used.

steps.text: Scroll to **How “supports $X” is worked out**, under **Can you?**.

Type your lender’s figures in the boxes on the right: debt coverage on the amortizing payment, debt coverage on the interest-only payment (leave it blank unless the lender uses it), loan-to-value and debt yield.
Untick **Lender uses** on any limit your lender doesn’t use. It turns grey and no longer counts.
If you have an appraisal, type it in **Appraised value**, with its date and a note. The loan-to-value then works on it instead of NOI ÷ cap rate.

marks.label: Your lender’s
marks.text: Type each limit here.

marks.label: Lender uses
marks.text: Unticked here: this lender doesn’t use debt yield.

marks.label: The smallest
marks.text: What the property supports now.

callouts.text: The limits and the appraisal are kept with this refinance for the whole team. **Back to the start** puts the limits back, and **Change history** lists every change.
If the group has your lender’s limits saved, pick it in **Lender preset** instead of typing. See [Use a lender preset](use-a-lender-preset).

steps.text: Scroll to **Proposed New Loan** and change **Term (yrs)**, **Amortization (yrs)**, **Interest-only (mo)** or **Closing (% of loan)** to your lender’s terms.

marks.label: Term (yrs)
marks.text: Years until the new loan is due.

marks.label: Amortization (yrs)
marks.text: Years the payment is figured over.

marks.label: Interest-only (mo)
marks.text: Months of interest-only payments first.

marks.label: Closing (% of loan)
marks.text: Closing costs.

marks.label: New monthly payment
marks.text: Compared with today’s.

steps.text: Open **Escrows & reserves** and **Additional fees** to add what the lender collects each month with the payment.

callouts.text: **Proposed New Loan** appears when the answer is **Refinance**, **Your decision** or a pay-down.

next.text: Make the proposed loan a loan.
Pick a lender’s saved limits instead of typing them.

pages.title: Use a lender preset
pages.description: Save a lender’s limits once, for the whole group, and pick them in any refinance.
pages.intro: A lender preset holds one lender’s numbers: its limits and which of them it uses, the rate types it lends at, its longest amortization and the penalty it usually asks on an extension. Pick it in a refinance instead of typing the numbers each time.

callouts.text: In the shared database, only the group’s admin adds or changes presets; anyone else gets “Only the group’s admin changes the lender presets”. Anyone can pick one.

steps.text: Open a refinance and scroll to **How “supports $X” is worked out**, in the colored verdict box. See [Run a refinance](run-a-refinance).
Click **Add a preset** next to **Lender preset**. Once the list has a preset, the link reads **Manage presets**.

marks.label: none yet
marks.text: No presets in the group’s list yet.

marks.label: Add a preset
marks.text: Opens the group’s list of lender presets.

marks.label: The limits
marks.text: Without a preset you type them here yourself.

steps.text: In the window, click **Add a preset**. An empty preset appears.
Type the lender’s name and its limits (**DSCR**, **IO**, **LTV**, **DY**), and tick the limits it uses.
Untick any rate type it doesn’t lend at, and fill in its longest amortization, its usual penalty on an extension, notes and the source.

marks.label: Name
marks.text: The lender (made-up here). A preset without a name is dropped when you save.

marks.label: Limits
marks.text: DSCR, IO, LTV and DY: here 1.30× / 70% / 8%.

marks.label: Uses
marks.text: The limits this lender uses.

marks.label: Rate types
marks.text: Floating unticked: this lender doesn’t lend floating.

marks.label: Save the list
marks.text: Saves it for the whole group.

steps.text: Click **Save the list**. **Close** instead drops your changes.
Pick the preset in **Lender preset**. The limits fill in from it, and what the property supports is worked out again.

marks.label: Lender preset
marks.text: Pick a lender, or “None — type the limits”.

marks.label: Its name
marks.text: The preset in use.

marks.label: The limits
marks.text: Filled from the preset.

marks.label: What the property supports
marks.text: On the preset’s limits.

steps.text: Check **Proposed rate** above it. A rate type the lender doesn’t allow is greyed, and clicking it says why instead of switching.

marks.label: Fixed
marks.text: Allowed.

marks.label: Floating (greyed)
marks.text: Not allowed by this preset. Clicking it shows “Example Agency (made-up): no floating”.

marks.label: Hybrid
marks.text: Allowed.

callouts.text: For an extension, pick today’s lender’s preset in the extension’s own limits. It also fills in the penalty that lender usually asks. See [Extend with today’s lender](extend-with-your-lender).
Type over a limit to change it for this deal only. The preset’s name then says “(changed here)”.

next.text: Type the rest of the lender’s quote.
Every box in the presets window.

pages.title: Plan what to push for a refinance
pages.description: Pick the amount the new loan must cover, tick what you would push, and see whether the NOI gets there.
pages.intro: **What to push — what it would get you** is your plan, not the lender’s. Pick the amount the new loan has to cover, tick Claude’s pushes and your own levers, and see whether the NOI they add covers it. The coverage, the verdict and the proposed loan follow what you tick.
before: The property’s underwriting approved, with Claude’s **What to push** — see [See what you can still push](use-what-to-push). Your own levers work without it.

steps.text: Open the property’s refinance and pick the **NOI basis** in **Coverage & value**. Each push counts on that basis. See [Run a refinance](run-a-refinance).
Scroll to **What to push — what it would get you**. Under **The amount to cover**, click what the new loan has to cover.

marks.label: Today’s payoff
marks.text: What you owe today plus the early-payoff penalty. The starting choice.

marks.label: No penalty — the last 12 months
marks.text: What you will owe 12 months before maturity, when there is no penalty.

marks.label: At maturity
marks.text: What you will owe when the loan matures. Picked here.

marks.label: The NOI you need
marks.text: The NOI that covers that amount, and how much more it is than today’s.

steps.text: Read the line under the buttons: the NOI that covers that amount at the proposed rate and the lender’s limits, and how far today’s NOI is from it.
Tick a push in the list. What it adds on your basis goes into the NOI.
To count something of your own, type its name and the dollars it adds a year under **Add your own lever**, then click **Add**. It is added ticked.

marks.label: Added to the NOI
marks.text: Everything ticked, on this basis.

marks.label: Covered — or still missing
marks.text: Whether the NOI now covers the amount.

marks.label: A push, ticked
marks.text: Claude’s, from What to push in Underwriting.

marks.label: Your lever
marks.text: Marked “yours”; × removes it.

steps.text: Read the line under the amount again: **covered**, with what is to spare, or how much NOI is **still missing**.

callouts.text: Your ticks, your levers and the amount to cover are kept with this refinance for the whole team.

steps.text: Click another **NOI basis** in **Coverage & value**. The same push counts its effect on that basis: it is worth less on an underwriting that already counts part of it.

marks.label: Its effect on each basis
marks.text: First on the basis picked (now In-place T12), then in-place, Safe and Aggressive.

marks.label: Added to the NOI
marks.text: Follows the basis.

next.text: Where the pushes come from, and what Claude checked.
Set the rate and the lender’s limits the NOI is measured at.
Every part of What to push, named.

pages.title: Extend with today’s lender
pages.description: Judge an extension with today’s lender, set its terms, and save it on today’s loan.
pages.intro: Instead of a new loan, today’s lender may keep the loan on new terms, usually after a pay-down so it fits the lender’s limits. The refinance judges the extension by the same rule as a new loan: can you, and should you? Saving it changes today’s loan, and you can undo it.

callouts.text: An extension is with one lender, one loan at a time. For a package of several loans, **Extend with today’s lender** is greyed.

before: Today’s lender’s quote: the rate, its limits, the penalty and the fee it asks.

steps.text: Open the loan’s refinance. See [Run a refinance](run-a-refinance).
Under **What kind of deal?**, click **Extend with today’s lender**. The verdict, the limits and the schedule below now judge the extension. **New loan** switches back, and each keeps its own figures.
In the verdict box, under **The extension’s rate**, pick the **Index** and type today’s lender’s **Spread (bps)**.
In the limits table under it, type today’s lender’s own limits, and untick **Lender uses** on any it doesn’t use. Here 1.11× amortizing and 1.35× interest-only (made-up).

marks.label: Amortizing coverage
marks.text: Today’s lender’s DSCR.

marks.label: Interest-only coverage
marks.text: Its coverage on the interest-only payment.

marks.label: Lender uses
marks.text: Untick a limit it doesn’t use.

marks.label: What today’s lender allows
marks.text: The smallest of the limits it uses.

callouts.text: If the group has today’s lender’s preset, pick it in **Lender preset** there instead. It fills in the limits and the penalty that lender usually asks.

steps.text: Scroll to **The extension’s terms**. Set **Today’s terms end on**, **Months on the new terms**, **Interest-only** and the amortization after it.
Pick what this lender asks in **Early-payoff penalty — this lender asks**, and set the **Extension fee**. Until you pick, the penalty is assumed to be on the pay-down only.

marks.label: Early-payoff penalty
marks.text: The full penalty, on the pay-down only, a part, or none.

marks.label: Extension fee
marks.text: In % of the extended amount, or dollars.

marks.label: Pay-down needed
marks.text: So the loan fits the lender’s limits.

marks.label: Cash needed
marks.text: Pay-down + penalty + fee.

marks.label: Assumed
marks.text: Confirm the penalty with the lender.

steps.text: Scroll back up to the verdict box. **Can you?** gives the pay-down the extension needs, and the last line says what to do and the cash it takes.

marks.label: The answer
marks.text: Here: Extend, with a pay-down.

marks.label: The pay-down
marks.text: What you will owe less what the lender’s limits allow.

marks.label: Should you?
marks.text: Yes here: the rate resets within 12 months.

marks.label: Bottom line
marks.text: What to do, with the cash it takes.

steps.text: Click **Save the extension** at the top. A box lists what will change.

marks.label: Save the extension?
marks.text: It asks first.

marks.label: What happens
marks.text: The new terms, the pay-down, the penalty, the new maturity, the status and the cash needed.

marks.label: Save the extension
marks.text: Saves it.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing changes.

steps.text: Click **Save the extension** in the box. Today’s loan stays the same record: from the date its terms end it has the new rate and term, the pay-down becomes a principal payment, and its status becomes Extended. Every changed field goes into the loan’s history.

callouts.text: **Save the extension** shows only when the answer is to extend. **Not yet** means nothing ends or resets within 12 months, so you decide closer to the date. **Don’t extend now** means the lower rate doesn’t pay for the penalty.

steps.text: Open the loan’s refinance again. It shows the saved extension.

marks.label: Extended with today’s lender
marks.text: The extension is saved on today’s loan.

marks.label: Saved
marks.text: When, and by whom. The loan’s own page has the extension too.

marks.label: What was saved
marks.text: The new terms, the pay-down, the new maturity and the cash it took.

marks.label: Undo the extension
marks.text: Puts today’s loan back as it was before.

marks.label: Change history
marks.text: The extension and every change before it.

steps.text: Click **Undo the extension**.

marks.label: Undo the extension?
marks.text: It asks first.

marks.label: What happens
marks.text: The loan goes back to its terms before the extension; the pay-down comes off the schedule; the history keeps both.

marks.label: Undo the extension
marks.text: Does it.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Keeps the extension.

steps.text: Click **Undo the extension** in the box. The rate, the maturity, the status and the schedule are put back, and the undo is in the history too.

next.text: Every box of the extension, named.
Set what the payment does at the reset.

pages.title: Refinance several loans together
pages.description: Refinance a senior and a mezzanine loan as one package, or put several properties under one new loan.
pages.intro: Loans that depend on one another are refinanced together: a property’s senior and mezzanine loans, or several properties under one new loan. The refinance works the same way, on the package’s total NOI and everything it owes.
before: A T12 for every property in the package — see [Upload a T12](upload-a-t12). Nothing is sized until each one has its T12.

sections.title: A senior and a mezzanine loan

steps.text: Click **Specific Property** and pick the property’s combined entry: its name followed by **senior + mezz**.
Click **Refi Calculator**. **Current debt** lists every loan on the property; one new loan pays them all off.

marks.label: The loans
marks.text: Here a senior and a mezzanine loan.

marks.label: Payoff balance
marks.text: Each loan at its own balance, added up.

marks.label: Current rate
marks.text: Weighted by what is owed on each.

sections.title: Several properties under one new loan

steps.text: On the **Portfolio** tab, click **Create a portfolio…** above the Coverage table.
Tick each property the new loan will secure. Each row shows what is owed and the NOI its refinance would use; the line under the list adds them up.

marks.label: Tick a property
marks.text: Each one the new loan will secure.

marks.label: Owes · NOI
marks.text: What is owed, and the NOI its refinance would use.

marks.label: The package
marks.text: The loans to pay off, what is owed and the NOI, together.

marks.label: Create the portfolio
marks.text: Needs at least two properties and one loan to pay off.

steps.text: Click **Create the portfolio**. The refinance opens for the whole package; nothing changes until you save.
In **NOI by property**, pick each property’s basis: **In-place T12**, or **Safe** or **Aggressive** once its underwriting is approved. The total, and everything below it, follows.

marks.label: Its basis
marks.text: The NOI this property counts with.

marks.label: NOI
marks.text: Its NOI on that basis.

marks.label: Total
marks.text: What the package is sized on.

steps.text: Read the verdict for the whole package. **Save as a loan** puts one new loan on all of the properties and pays off every loan on them. See [Save the refinance as a loan](save-the-refinance).

callouts.text: A ticked property with no T12 stops the package: the screen says **No T12 yet** and offers to upload it in Underwriting. A typed NOI never counts for a refinance.
**What to push** lists each property’s pushes under its name; tick them to see what the package could carry. See [Plan what to push for a refinance](plan-what-to-push).

next.text: Add a loan that already covers several properties.
Every part of a package refinance, named.

pages.title: The refinance page
pages.description: Every figure and control on a loan’s refinance: today’s loan, coverage, what to push, the verdict, the rate and limits, presets, the proposed loan, the extension and packages.
pages.intro: The refinance opens from a loan’s page with **Refi Calculator** and takes its place. From the top: today’s loan and the kind of deal, coverage and value, what to push, the verdict with the proposed rate and the lender’s limits, then the proposed loan or the extension. The pictures use the app’s sample loans with made-up T12s. Point at a number, on the picture or in the list, to find it.

sections.title: Today’s loan
sections.text: The top of the refinance: the buttons, what you owe today, and the kind of deal.

views.title: The refinance screen
views.text: Everything is worked out live: change a box and the answers update at once. Your choices (the lender’s limits, an appraisal, the kind of deal) are kept with the property for the whole team.

marks.label: Refinance Analysis
marks.text: The loan, and the question: should you refinance?

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Back to the loan’s page. Closing saves nothing and loses nothing.

marks.label: Save as a loan
marks.text: Shown when there is a loan to propose. Saves it as a new loan and marks today’s loan Paid off (refinanced); it asks first. With a pay-down it says the cash you pay in. See [Save the refinance as a loan](save-the-refinance).

marks.label: Refi Calculator (greyed)
marks.text: Greyed while the refinance is open.

marks.label: What kind of deal?
marks.text: A new loan, or an extension with today’s lender.

views.title: Current Loan
views.text: The facts of today’s loan, from its record.

marks.label: Payoff balance
marks.text: What you owe today: what a new loan has to pay off.

marks.label: Current rate
marks.text: Today’s interest rate.

marks.label: Monthly P&I
marks.text: Today’s monthly principal and interest.

marks.label: Remaining
marks.text: Months until today’s loan ends.

marks.label: Matures
marks.text: The date today’s loan is due.

marks.label: Rate reset
marks.text: For a hybrid loan: when the fixed rate ends, what it resets to and the new payment.

views.title: What kind of deal?
views.text: Pick this first: everything below follows it. Each kind keeps its own limits, so switching back and forth loses nothing.

marks.label: New loan
marks.text: The verdict, the limits and the schedule below are a new loan’s, which replaces today’s loan(s).

marks.label: Extend with today’s lender
marks.text: Judge an extension instead: today’s lender keeps the loan on new terms, perhaps after a pay-down. See [The extension](ref-refinance#the-extension).

sections.title: Coverage & value
sections.text: Today’s loan measured on the property’s NOI: the figures a lender looks at first. They are screening estimates; confirm them with the loan documents and a rate sheet.

marks.label: NOI basis
marks.text: Which NOI the refinance is sized on: here In-place T12, from the property’s T12 (made-up). Safe and Aggressive are greyed until the underwriting is approved.

marks.label: Annual NOI
marks.text: The yearly NOI used: from the T12, or the approved underwriting. A typed NOI never sizes a refinance.

marks.label: Cap rate
marks.text: Values the property: value = NOI ÷ cap rate.

marks.label: Est. value
marks.text: The estimated value. An appraisal you type replaces it.

marks.label: LTV today
marks.text: Loan-to-value: what you owe ÷ the value.

marks.label: Debt service today
marks.text: A year of today’s payments.

marks.label: DSCR today
marks.text: Debt coverage: NOI ÷ a year of payments. Lenders usually want 1.25× or more.

marks.label: Interest-only DSCR
marks.text: Coverage on an interest-only payment, which some lenders size on.

marks.label: Debt yield today
marks.text: NOI ÷ what you owe, which insurance companies and CMBS lenders look at.

marks.label: Coverage today
marks.text: Whether today’s coverage clears your DSCR floor.

marks.label: Cap rate
marks.text: Opens a small window to change the cap rate.

marks.label: Credit tier
marks.text: How a lender would grade today’s numbers. Below the floor, the line under it says which test fails; a strong tier takes basis points off the proposed spread.

marks.label: Why it is below the floor
marks.text: Each test that fails against your floor or ceiling: DSCR, LTV, debt yield. Shown only when one fails.

marks.label: Exit cost — penalty type
marks.text: How the early-payoff penalty is worked out. See Exit cost below.

marks.label: Exit cost
marks.text: The early-payoff penalty in dollars today (and as a % of the balance).

marks.label: Capital stack
marks.text: Links a mezzanine or senior loan on the same property. See Capital stack below.

marks.label: How these are worked out
marks.text: The formulas behind the figures above.

views.title: Cap rate
views.text: **Cap rate** changes only the cap rate that values the property. The NOI comes from the T12 or the approved underwriting, picked with the NOI basis; it is never typed here.

marks.label: Refinance — cap rate
marks.text: This window changes the cap rate only.

marks.label: Where the NOI comes from
marks.text: The T12, or the approved underwriting: the NOI basis on the Coverage card.

marks.label: Cap rate (%)
marks.text: Value = NOI ÷ cap rate; it sets the loan-to-value.

marks.label: Continue
marks.text: Saves the cap rate and updates the whole analysis.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes without changing anything.

views.title: Exit cost
views.text: Paying today’s loan off early usually costs a penalty. The app estimates it from the type of penalty in the loan; **assumed** means nobody has confirmed the type yet.

marks.label: Penalty type
marks.text: Yield Maintenance (the default), Step-down (a % of the balance that falls each year), Defeasance (a quoted figure), or Open / at par (no penalty). Picking one confirms it and saves it on the loan.

marks.label: Assumed
marks.text: Shown until you pick the type: the estimate uses yield maintenance.

marks.label: Prepay basis
marks.text: How the estimate was worked out; for yield maintenance, today’s Treasury, the months left and the 1% floor.

marks.label: Exit cost
marks.text: The estimated penalty in dollars. Confirm the real figure from the loan documents.

marks.label: As % of balance
marks.text: The same penalty as a share of what you owe.

views.title: Step-down
views.text: A step-down penalty asks for this year’s % of the balance.

marks.label: Step-down
marks.text: Picked here.

marks.label: This year’s step-down
marks.text: This year’s %, for example 3 in year 1 of a 3-2-1 schedule. The exit cost follows.

views.title: Defeasance
views.text: A defeasance takes the figure you were quoted by the lender or the consultant. Until you type one, a yield-maintenance estimate stands in.

marks.label: Defeasance
marks.text: Picked here.

marks.label: Quoted figure
marks.text: The defeasance cost you were quoted, in dollars.

views.title: Capital stack
views.text: When the property also has a mezzanine (or senior) loan, link it here: leverage and coverage are then read on the combined debt.

marks.label: Link a loan
marks.text: The other loan on the same property (None = this loan alone). Agency senior loans don’t allow subordinate debt.

views.title: The NOI basis
views.text: Villages of Whitewater has a made-up T12 and an approved underwriting, so its refinance can be sized on three NOIs. Pick one; everything below follows, and the pick is kept with this refinance for the whole team.

marks.label: In-place T12
marks.text: The NOI as the property runs today, from its T12.

marks.label: Safe underwriting
marks.text: The approved Safe underwriting: the T12 with the changes and stories you approved, after replacement reserves. The starting choice once it is approved.

marks.label: Aggressive underwriting
marks.text: The approved Aggressive version, after reserves.

marks.label: Which months
marks.text: How the T12’s NOI was worked out.

marks.label: What it is sized on
marks.text: Which NOI the analysis uses, and who approved the underwriting and when. Without an approved underwriting, only In-place T12 is offered.

sections.title: What to push
sections.text: Your planning tool, not the lender’s: tick what you would push, pick the amount you need to cover, and see what loan it gets you. The pushes are Claude’s, from **What to push** in Underwriting. See [Plan what to push for a refinance](plan-what-to-push).

views.title: What to push — what it would get you
views.text: Each push has three effects (on the in-place T12, on Safe and on Aggressive), net of what each already counts. Ticking one adds its effect on the NOI basis picked above.

marks.label: What to push — what it would get you
marks.text: Your plan: the coverage, the verdict and the proposed loan follow what you tick.

marks.label: The amount to cover
marks.text: What the loan has to cover, and the NOI that covers it. See the next picture.

marks.label: A push
marks.text: Tick to add it to the NOI used here; untick to take it out.

marks.label: Its effects
marks.text: First what it adds on the basis picked (here Safe), then on each basis: in-place, Safe, Aggressive. The same push is worth less on an underwriting that already counts part of it.

marks.label: Your own lever — name
marks.text: Something you expect to add, for example paid parking.

marks.label: Your own lever — dollars a year
marks.text: What it adds a year. It counts the same on any basis; a negative amount takes NOI away.

marks.label: Add
marks.text: Adds your lever to the list, ticked.

views.title: The amount to cover
views.text: What the new loan has to cover. The line under it says the NOI that covers it at the proposed rate and the lender’s limits, and how far today’s NOI is from it.

marks.label: Today’s payoff
marks.text: What you owe today plus the early-payoff penalty. The starting choice.

marks.label: No penalty — the last 12 months
marks.text: What you will owe 12 months before maturity, when the loan can be paid off without a penalty (today’s payoff if it matures within 12 months).

marks.label: At maturity
marks.text: What you will owe when the loan matures, before its final payment.

marks.label: What it is
marks.text: What the amount picked is made of.

marks.label: The NOI you need
marks.text: The NOI that covers the amount on the basis picked, and how much more that is than today’s.

views.title: Ticked
views.text: A push ticked and a lever of your own added (made-up): the card says what they add to the NOI, and the line under the amount whether that covers it.

marks.label: Added to the NOI
marks.text: What the ticked pushes and your levers add on this basis.

marks.label: Covered — or still missing
marks.text: Whether the NOI now covers the amount, with what is to spare or what is still missing.

marks.label: Ticked push
marks.text: Counted now.

marks.label: Your lever
marks.text: Marked “yours”; tick or untick it like Claude’s.
Removes your lever.

sections.title: The verdict
sections.text: The colored box answers two questions in order: can the property support a loan the size of what you owe, and is it worth doing? The proposed rate and amount, and how the answer is worked out, are inside it.

views.title: Act before … — pay down
views.text: Queens Gate’s rate resets within 12 months and the property can’t support what you owe. The box says so first, with the date, and what it takes: the pay-down to refinance at these limits, or an extension with today’s lender.

marks.label: The answer
marks.text: Act before the reset — pay down $X. The other answers: Refinance, Your decision, Don’t refinance.

marks.label: You owe (payoff)
marks.text: What a new loan has to pay off.

marks.label: Property supports
marks.text: The biggest loan the property supports at the proposed rate and the lender’s limits.

marks.label: Today’s loan rate
marks.text: With the reset ahead: what it resets to, and when.

marks.label: Proposed loan rate
marks.text: The new loan’s rate, from the rate boxes below.

marks.label: When
marks.text: What is ending: the rate reset (with the new payment) or the maturity.

marks.label: To refinance
marks.text: The pay-down a new loan needs: what you owe less what the property supports.

marks.label: To extend
marks.text: The pay-down today’s lender would need at its limits, and the cash it takes. Pick **Extend with today’s lender** to see it or to fill in its terms.

marks.label: Proposed rate
marks.text: The new loan’s rate type, index and spread. See [Rate & amount](ref-refinance#rate-amount).

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: Starts at what the property supports; type a smaller amount to test it. The line under it shows that loan’s coverage, LTV and debt yield.

marks.label: Can you?
marks.text: Stage one: can the property support a loan the size of what you owe? Here no, and why.

marks.label: How “supports $X” is worked out
marks.text: The NOI, rate, payment and value behind the figure, and the lender’s four limits. See [How much it supports](ref-refinance#how-much-it-supports).

marks.label: Bottom line
marks.text: What to do, in one line.

views.title: Refinance
views.text: The Mews at Princeton, with the lender’s spread typed as 0 for the example: the property supports more than you owe, and the lower rate saves more interest than the early-payoff penalty.

marks.label: Refinance
marks.text: Both answers are yes.

marks.label: You owe (payoff)
marks.text: What a new loan has to pay off.

marks.label: Property supports
marks.text: The biggest loan the property supports at the proposed rate and the lender’s limits.

marks.label: Today’s loan rate
marks.text: The rate today’s loan charges now.

marks.label: Proposed loan rate
marks.text: The new loan’s rate, from the rate boxes below.

marks.label: Proposed rate
marks.text: The new loan’s rate type, index and spread. See [Rate & amount](ref-refinance#rate-amount).

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: Type a smaller amount to test it. The line under it shows that loan’s coverage, LTV and debt yield.

marks.label: Can you? Yes
marks.text: The property supports at least what you owe.

marks.label: How “supports $X” is worked out
marks.text: The NOI, rate, payment and value behind the figure, and the lender’s four limits. See [How much it supports](ref-refinance#how-much-it-supports).

marks.label: Should you? Yes
marks.text: Your rule: the new rate saves more interest (until today’s loan ends) than the penalty, or today’s loan ends within 12 months anyway. When the saving doesn’t cover the penalty but the property can refinance, the box turns amber: Your decision.

marks.label: Refinance.
marks.text: The proposed loan appears below, with **Save as a loan** at the top.

views.title: Your decision
views.text: The Mews at Princeton with a 20 bps spread and a bigger loan of $135,000,000 (made-up). The lower rate no longer saves as much as the penalty, but the new loan pays out more than 20% of what you owe in cash, even after the penalty. So the app shows both choices. With the same rate and a loan only the size of what you owe, the answer is Don’t refinance.

marks.label: Your decision
marks.text: The property can refinance, and it is worth it only for the cash.

marks.label: You owe (payoff)
marks.text: What a new loan has to pay off.

marks.label: Property supports
marks.text: The biggest loan the property supports at the proposed rate and the lender’s limits.

marks.label: Today’s loan rate
marks.text: The rate today’s loan charges now.

marks.label: Proposed loan rate
marks.text: The new loan’s rate, from the rate boxes below.

marks.label: Proposed rate
marks.text: The new loan’s rate type, index and spread. See [Rate & amount](ref-refinance#rate-amount).

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: Type a smaller amount to test it. The line under it shows that loan’s coverage, LTV and debt yield.

marks.label: Can you? Yes
marks.text: The property supports at least what you owe.

marks.label: How “supports $X” is worked out
marks.text: The NOI, rate, payment and value behind the figure, and the lender’s four limits. See [How much it supports](ref-refinance#how-much-it-supports).

marks.label: Should you? Your decision
marks.text: The interest saved is less than the penalty, but the cash out is more than 20% of what you owe.

marks.label: Refinance now — with $X cash
marks.text: The cash left after paying off what you owe and the penalty. To take it, click **Save as a loan — Refinance now** at the top.

marks.label: Wait until …
marks.text: Or keep today’s loan until it ends; nothing changes.

marks.label: Your decision.
marks.text: The choice is yours. Lowering the amount so far that the cash no longer covers the penalty is refused with “You can’t do that”.

views.title: Don’t refinance
views.text: The Mint: the property supports less than you owe, and its loan doesn’t end or reset within 12 months, so there is nothing to do yet.

marks.label: Don’t refinance
marks.text: The answer.

marks.label: You owe (payoff)
marks.text: What a new loan has to pay off.

marks.label: Property supports
marks.text: The biggest loan the property supports at the proposed rate and the lender’s limits.

marks.label: Today’s loan rate
marks.text: The rate today’s loan charges now.

marks.label: Proposed loan rate
marks.text: The new loan’s rate, from the rate boxes below.

marks.label: Proposed rate
marks.text: The new loan’s rate type, index and spread. See [Rate & amount](ref-refinance#rate-amount).

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: Type a smaller amount to test it. The line under it shows that loan’s coverage, LTV and debt yield.

marks.label: Can you? No
marks.text: What caps it, and what would change it: NOI rising, the rate falling, or a pay-down.

marks.label: How “supports $X” is worked out
marks.text: The NOI, rate, payment and value behind the figure, and the lender’s four limits. See [How much it supports](ref-refinance#how-much-it-supports).

marks.label: Bottom line
marks.text: Don’t refinance: the property can’t support a loan the size of the payoff yet.

views.title: No T12 yet
views.text: Avalon Norwalk has no T12. A refinance is sized on the T12 and the underwriting made from it, never on a typed NOI, so nothing is sized.

marks.label: No T12 yet
marks.text: This property has no T12 uploaded.

marks.label: Why nothing is sized
marks.text: A refinance is sized on the T12 and the underwriting made from it.

marks.label: Upload its T12 in Underwriting
marks.text: Closes the refinance and opens Underwriting on this property, ready for its T12.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Back to the loan’s page.

sections.title: Rate & amount
sections.text: Inside the verdict box: the new loan’s rate type, index and spread, and its amount. It starts from today’s loan’s type and a usual spread; type your lender’s quote and everything above and below updates at once.

views.title: Hybrid
views.text: A fixed period, then adjustable.

marks.label: Fixed
marks.text: One rate for the whole term: a Treasury matched to the term + the lender’s spread.

marks.label: Floating
marks.text: An index (SOFR, Prime …) + a margin, changing as the index moves.

marks.label: Hybrid
marks.text: Fixed for the first years, then adjustable.

marks.label: Index (fixed period)
marks.text: The Treasury the fixed period is priced on. The list holds every rate the app has; **Fetch live rate** at the top refreshes them.

marks.label: Spread (bps)
marks.text: The lender’s quote in basis points (100 bps = 1%).

marks.label: Index (adjustable)
marks.text: What the rate follows after the fixed period.

marks.label: Margin (bps)
marks.text: The lender’s margin over that index.

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: Up to what the property supports; lowering it shows the cash you’d pay in.

marks.label: Rate (fixed period)
marks.text: The index today + the spread. “Built-in rate — fetch to update” means the index is the app’s own figure until you click **Fetch live rate**. The yellow “starting spread” tag says where the starting spread came from (your recent loans of this kind); it goes once you type the lender’s quote.

marks.label: Monthly payment (fixed period)
marks.text: The payment in the fixed years. The verdict and the limits use this rate.

marks.label: Monthly payment (after)
marks.text: The payment after the fixed period if the index stays where it is today, for information only.

marks.label: At this amount
marks.text: The proposed loan’s coverage, interest-only coverage, LTV and debt yield at the amount typed.

views.title: Floating
views.text: Pick the index and type the lender’s margin. The rate is today’s index + the margin.

marks.label: Floating
marks.text: Picked.

marks.label: Index
marks.text: SOFR (overnight or 30-day average), Prime, or a Treasury: every rate the app has.

marks.label: Spread (bps)
marks.text: The lender’s margin over the index, in basis points.

marks.label: Rate floor (%)
marks.text: The lowest the rate can go, whatever the index does. Empty = no floor.

marks.label: Rate cap (%)
marks.text: The highest the rate can go. Empty = no cap.

marks.label: Cap cost (bps/yr)
marks.text: The yearly cost of an interest-rate cap, which floating lenders often require. It starts at 0 until you buy one.

marks.label: Rate
marks.text: Today’s index (and the day it was set) + the spread.

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: The new loan’s amount. Switching the rate type works out what the property supports again.

views.title: Fixed
views.text: The Treasury that matches the term, plus the lender’s spread.

marks.label: Fixed
marks.text: Picked.

marks.label: Index
marks.text: The Treasury matched to the loan’s term. Change it if the lender prices on another.

marks.label: Spread (bps)
marks.text: The lender’s spread.

marks.label: Rate
marks.text: The Treasury today + the spread: one rate for the whole term.

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: The new loan’s amount.

marks.label: At this amount
marks.text: That loan’s coverage, LTV and debt yield.

sections.title: How much it supports
sections.text: How “supports $X” is worked out, under **Can you?**: the NOI, the rate, the payment and the value, and the four limits a lender sizes a loan on. Each limit allows a loan; the smallest of the ones your lender uses is what the property supports. Your figures are kept with this refinance for the whole team.

marks.label: NOI
marks.text: The NOI used, and where it comes from.

marks.label: Rate
marks.text: The proposed loan’s rate (index + spread).

marks.label: Payment
marks.text: How the payment is figured: amortizing, interest-only months.

marks.label: Value
marks.text: NOI ÷ cap rate, or the appraisal once you type one. The loan-to-value limit works on this.

marks.label: Appraised value
marks.text: Type an appraisal to use it instead of NOI ÷ cap rate.

marks.label: Dated
marks.text: The appraisal’s date, kept with it.

marks.label: Note
marks.text: Who appraised it, or any note.

marks.label: Lender preset
marks.text: A lender’s saved limits. See [Lender presets](ref-refinance#lender-presets).

marks.label: Lender uses
marks.text: Tick the limits this lender uses; an unticked one is greyed and doesn’t count.

marks.label: Lender limit
marks.text: The limit’s name, how its loan is worked out, and (grey) that loan’s coverage, LTV and debt yield.

marks.label: Debt coverage, amortizing
marks.text: NOI ÷ (this × the loan constant). Lenders often ask 1.20–1.35×.

marks.label: Debt coverage, interest-only
marks.text: Leave blank (not used) unless the lender sizes on the interest-only payment.

marks.label: Loan-to-value
marks.text: The most it lends, as a % of the value.

marks.label: Debt yield
marks.text: The least NOI ÷ loan it accepts.

marks.label: Loan it allows
marks.text: The biggest loan each limit allows on its own.

marks.label: Binds
marks.text: The limit that sets the amount: the smallest one used.

marks.label: The smallest
marks.text: The smallest loan of the limits used: what the property supports.

marks.label: Headroom
marks.text: How much room is left before the next limit would bind instead.

marks.label: Change history
marks.text: Every change to this refinance’s limits, appraisal and deal: when, who, old → new.

views.title: An appraisal and the lender’s own limits
views.text: Typed: an appraised value (a made-up $65,000,000), and Debt yield unticked because this lender doesn’t use it. The loan-to-value now works on the appraisal, and the unticked line is greyed.

marks.label: Value
marks.text: Now the appraisal, with its note.

marks.label: Use NOI ÷ cap rate instead
marks.text: Drops the appraisal and goes back to NOI ÷ cap rate.

marks.label: Appraised value
marks.text: Clear the box to go back to NOI ÷ cap rate.

marks.label: Note
marks.text: Here “Example appraiser (made-up)”.

marks.label: Loan-to-value
marks.text: 75% of the appraisal.

marks.label: Not used by this lender
marks.text: Greyed; it no longer counts. Tick it to use it again. At least one limit must stay ticked.

marks.label: The smallest of the limits this lender uses
marks.text: Only the ticked limits count.

marks.label: Back to the start
marks.text: Puts the limits back to 1.25× / 75% / 7%, all used. Shown once you have changed them.

marks.label: Change history
marks.text: Lists the changes just made.

views.title: Change history
views.text: Every change to this refinance (limits, appraisal, kind of deal, extension terms) with who made it and when.

marks.label: Refinance — change history
marks.text: This refinance’s own list.

marks.label: A change
marks.text: When, what (for example Refinance · appraised value), old → new, who, and where it came from.
Closes the list.

sections.title: Lender presets
sections.text: A list of lenders’ limits kept for the whole group, so you pick a lender instead of typing its numbers. The list starts empty; next to **Lender preset**, the admin sees **Add a preset**, later **Manage presets**. Only the group’s admin edits the list (anyone else gets “Only the group’s admin changes the lender presets”); anyone can pick a preset. See [Use a lender preset](use-a-lender-preset).

views.title: The presets window
views.text: Each preset is one lender. Nothing is saved until **Save the list**.

marks.label: Name
marks.text: The lender, for example Fannie Mae. A preset without a name is dropped when you save.

marks.label: DSCR
marks.text: Its debt coverage on the amortizing payment.

marks.label: IO
marks.text: Its coverage on an interest-only payment (blank if it doesn’t use one).

marks.label: LTV
marks.text: Its most loan-to-value, in %.

marks.label: DY
marks.text: Its least debt yield, in %.

marks.label: Remove
marks.text: Takes this preset off the list.

marks.label: Uses
marks.text: The limits this lender uses.

marks.label: Interest-only sizing
marks.text: Tick if it sizes a loan that is interest-only for its whole term on the interest-only payment.

marks.label: Rate types
marks.text: The rate types it lends at; an unticked one is greyed in the refinance.

marks.label: Longest amortization
marks.text: In years.

marks.label: Penalty on an extension
marks.text: What this lender usually asks when it extends a loan: the full penalty, on the pay-down only, a part (% or $), or none.

marks.label: Part (%)
marks.text: For a part (%): the share of the full penalty (here 50%). A part ($) asks for a dollar amount instead.

marks.label: Notes
marks.text: Anything else worth remembering about this lender.

marks.label: Source
marks.text: Where the numbers came from, and when.

marks.label: Add a preset
marks.text: Adds another lender.

marks.label: Save the list
marks.text: Saves the list for the whole group and closes the window.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes without saving; the changes are dropped.

views.title: A preset picked
views.text: Picked for this refinance: the limits fill in from the preset, the table names it, and a rate type the lender doesn’t allow is greyed in the rate boxes (clicking it says why).

marks.label: Lender preset
marks.text: Pick a lender, or “None — type the limits”.

marks.label: Its name
marks.text: The preset in use; “(changed here)” once you change a limit by hand.

marks.label: Manage presets
marks.text: Edit the group’s list (admin only).

marks.label: What it allows
marks.text: The rate types this lender lends at, and its longest amortization.

marks.label: The limits
marks.text: Filled from the preset (here 1.30× / 70% / 8%). Type over one and its name says “changed here”.

marks.label: What the property supports
marks.text: Worked out again on the preset’s limits.

sections.title: The proposed loan
sections.text: Shown when the answer is **Refinance**, **Your decision** or a pay-down: the new loan’s terms and its payment schedule. It matches today’s term and interest-only period, priced at today’s rate; every box is editable and the verdict updates as you type. **Save as a loan** at the top saves it; see [Save the refinance as a loan](save-the-refinance).

marks.label: Loan amount
marks.text: Set in the verdict box above.

marks.label: Term (yrs)
marks.text: Years until the new loan is due.

marks.label: Amortization (yrs)
marks.text: Years the payment is figured over.

marks.label: Interest-only (mo)
marks.text: Months of interest-only payments first.

marks.label: Closing (% of loan)
marks.text: Closing costs, as a % of the loan.

marks.label: New monthly payment
marks.text: The first payment, and how it compares with today’s.

marks.label: vs your current
marks.text: Today’s monthly payment, and how much the new one saves (or costs) each month.

marks.label: Escrows & reserves
marks.text: Click to open: tax and insurance escrows, replacement and TI/LC reserves, ground lease, other escrows.

marks.label: Additional fees
marks.text: Click to open: servicing, trustee and other fees.

marks.label: Amortization schedule
marks.text: Every payment of the new loan: rate, interest, payment, principal and balance; interest-only months are marked IO. Scroll inside the box for the rest.

views.title: Escrows, reserves and fees
views.text: Opened: the monthly escrows, reserves and fees that come with the new loan’s payment. Every box here is added to the monthly payment.

marks.label: Tax escrow
marks.text: Monthly real-estate-tax escrow, in dollars a month.

marks.label: Insurance escrow
marks.text: Monthly insurance escrow.

marks.label: Replacement reserve
marks.text: Monthly replacement reserve.

marks.label: TI/LC reserve
marks.text: Tenant improvements and leasing commissions (commercial).

marks.label: Ground lease
marks.text: A ground-lease payment, if any.

marks.label: Servicing fee
marks.text: The servicer’s monthly fee.

marks.label: Other escrow 1
marks.text: Any other monthly escrow.

marks.label: Other escrow 2
marks.text: A second one.

marks.label: Trustee fee
marks.text: The trustee’s monthly fee.

marks.label: Other fee 1
marks.text: Any other monthly fee.

marks.label: Other fee 2
marks.text: A second one.

sections.title: The extension
sections.text: With **Extend with today’s lender** picked, everything below judges the extension instead of a new loan: its own verdict, rate, limits, terms and schedule. Saving it, and undoing it, are shown in [Extend with today’s lender](extend-with-your-lender).

marks.label: Extend with today’s lender
marks.text: Picked.

marks.label: Save the extension
marks.text: Shown when the answer is to extend. Saves the extension on today’s loan, with the pay-down it needs; it asks first.

views.title: The extension’s verdict
views.text: The same rule as a new loan, applied to the extension: the pay-down it needs to fit today’s lender’s limits, and whether it is worth doing.

marks.label: The answer
marks.text: Extend — pay down $X, or Not yet, or Don’t extend now.

marks.label: You’ll owe on …
marks.text: What you will owe on the day today’s terms end.

marks.label: Today’s lender allows
marks.text: The biggest loan today’s lender’s limits allow at the extension’s rate.

marks.label: Today’s loan rate
marks.text: With the reset ahead.

marks.label: Extension rate
marks.text: The index + today’s lender’s spread.

marks.label: Index
marks.text: What the extension’s rate floats on: every rate the app has.

marks.label: Spread (bps)
marks.text: Today’s lender’s quote over the index.

marks.label: Can you?
marks.text: Yes, with or without a pay-down.

marks.label: The pay-down
marks.text: What you will owe less what the lender’s limits allow, and which limit sets it.

marks.label: Today’s lender’s limits
marks.text: The limits table for the extension, kept apart from a new loan’s. See the next picture.

marks.label: Should you?
marks.text: Yes when today’s loan ends or resets within 12 months; Not yet when nothing ends or resets within 12 months; otherwise yes only when the lower rate saves more than the penalty.

marks.label: Bottom line
marks.text: What to do, with the cash it takes: pay-down + penalty + fee.

views.title: Today’s lender’s limits
views.text: Today’s lender’s own limits for the extension (here 1.11× amortizing and 1.35× interest-only, made-up), kept with the property apart from a new loan’s.

marks.label: Amortizing coverage
marks.text: Today’s lender’s DSCR.

marks.label: Interest-only coverage
marks.text: Its coverage on the interest-only payment.

marks.label: Loan-to-value
marks.text: Today’s lender’s most loan-to-value, here on the appraisal.

marks.label: Debt yield
marks.text: Its least debt yield.

marks.label: Lender uses
marks.text: Untick a limit today’s lender doesn’t use.

marks.label: Lender preset
marks.text: Today’s lender’s preset, if the group has one. It also fills in the penalty that lender usually asks. **Manage presets** edits the list (admin only).

marks.label: Appraised value
marks.text: Shared with the new loan’s: one appraisal for the property (here a made-up $65,000,000).

marks.label: What today’s lender allows
marks.text: The smallest of the limits it uses; the binding one is marked BINDS.

marks.label: Interest-only hint
marks.text: The extension is interest-only for its whole term: untick the amortizing line if the lender sizes on the interest-only payment.

marks.label: Back to the new loan’s limits
marks.text: Drops today’s lender’s own limits and uses the new loan’s again.

marks.label: Change history
marks.text: Every change to the refinance, these limits included.

views.title: The extension’s terms
views.text: When today’s terms end, how long the new terms run, interest-only, the amortization after it, the lender’s penalty and the fee, and what it all adds up to.

marks.label: Today’s terms end on
marks.text: Starts at the payment before the rate resets (or the maturity).

marks.label: Months on the new terms
marks.text: How long the extension runs.

marks.label: Interest-only
marks.text: The whole term, the first N months, or none.

marks.label: Amortization
marks.text: Months the payment is figured over after interest-only.

marks.label: Early-payoff penalty
marks.text: What this lender asks: the full penalty, on the pay-down only, a part, or none. Until you pick, it assumes on the pay-down.

marks.label: Extension fee in
marks.text: % of the extended amount, or dollars.

marks.label: Extension fee
marks.text: The fee.

marks.label: Pay-down needed
marks.text: What you pay down so the loan fits the lender’s limits.

marks.label: Extended amount
marks.text: What you owe after the pay-down.

marks.label: At this amount
marks.text: The extended loan’s coverage, interest-only coverage, LTV and debt yield.

marks.label: Penalty
marks.text: In dollars, how it was worked out, and the full penalty today.

marks.label: Assumed
marks.text: Until you pick what this lender asks, the penalty is assumed to be on the pay-down only. Confirm it with the lender.

marks.label: Extension fee
marks.text: The fee in dollars.

marks.label: Cash needed
marks.text: Pay-down + penalty + fee.

marks.label: First payment
marks.text: The date and amount of the first payment on the new terms.

marks.label: New maturity
marks.text: When the extended loan is due.

marks.label: Earlier than today’s
marks.text: A warning: these terms would end before today’s loan does. Type more months if that isn’t what you mean.

views.title: Penalty: a part of it
views.text: **A part (%)** asks what share of the full penalty the lender wants. **The first N months** of interest-only asks how many months.

marks.label: Part of the full penalty (%)
marks.text: Here 40% of today’s full penalty.

marks.label: Interest-only months
marks.text: How many months are interest-only (shown when you pick The first N months).

marks.label: Penalty
marks.text: Now 40% of the full penalty, no longer assumed.

marks.label: Cash needed
marks.text: Follows at once.

views.title: Penalty and fee in dollars
views.text: **A part ($)** asks for the penalty the lender quotes, in dollars; the fee can be in dollars too. Here a made-up $100,000 penalty and a $25,000 fee.

marks.label: A part — a dollar amount
marks.text: The other choices: the full penalty, on the pay-down only, a part (%), none.

marks.label: Penalty the lender asks ($)
marks.text: The lender’s figure.

marks.label: Extension fee in dollars
marks.text: Or % of the extended amount.

marks.label: Fee
marks.text: Counted in the cash needed.

views.title: The payment schedule with the extension
views.text: From today to the new maturity: the pay-down on the date today’s terms end, where the extension starts, and its months shaded.

marks.label: From today to …
marks.text: The whole schedule with the extension in place.

marks.label: Paid down
marks.text: The pay-down, as a principal payment.

marks.label: Extension starts
marks.text: The first payment on the new terms.

marks.label: Extension months
marks.text: Shaded: the new rate and terms.

views.title: Not yet
views.text: The Mews at Princeton: today’s lender’s limits cover what you’ll owe, but nothing ends or resets within 12 months, so the answer is Not yet and there is no **Save the extension**. When a lower rate doesn’t pay for the penalty, the answer is Don’t extend now.

marks.label: Not yet
marks.text: Today’s terms end more than 12 months from now.

marks.label: Can you? Yes
marks.text: Today’s lender’s limits allow more than you’ll owe: no pay-down needed.

marks.label: Should you? Not yet
marks.text: When today’s terms end, and that nothing ends or resets within 12 months.

marks.label: Bottom line
marks.text: Not yet: decide closer to the date.

sections.title: Several loans together
sections.text: A property’s senior and mezzanine loans refinance as one package; **Create a portfolio…** puts several properties under one new loan. An extension isn’t offered for a package. See [Refinance several loans together](refinance-together).

views.title: Senior + mezz: the whole property
views.text: The property’s combined entry under **Specific Property** (its name followed by **senior + mezz**), then **Refi Calculator**: one new loan pays off both. Here Avalon White Plains, with a made-up T12.

marks.label: The loans
marks.text: Every loan on the property, refinanced together (they depend on one another).

marks.label: Payoff balance
marks.text: Each loan at its own balance, added up.

marks.label: Monthly payments
marks.text: Today’s payments on all of them.

marks.label: Current rate
marks.text: The loans’ rate together, weighted by what is owed on each.

marks.label: Remaining
marks.text: Months until the first of them ends.

marks.label: Matures
marks.text: When the first of them is due.

views.title: Create a portfolio…
views.text: On the Portfolio tab, above the Coverage table. Tick every property the one new loan will secure. Nothing changes until you save the new loan on the next screen.

marks.label: Find a property
marks.text: Type to narrow the list.

marks.label: Tick a property
marks.text: Each property the new loan will secure.

marks.label: Owes · NOI
marks.text: What is owed on the property, and the NOI its refinance would use: its T12 (In-place T12), or its Safe underwriting once approved.

marks.label: The package
marks.text: How many are ticked, the loans to pay off and what is owed, and the NOI together (or which ticked property has no T12).

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes the list.

marks.label: Create the portfolio
marks.text: Opens the refinance of the ticked properties together. It needs at least two, and at least one loan to pay off.

views.title: NOI by property
views.text: The same refinance screen, for the whole package. Each property has its own row and its own NOI basis; the package is sized on the total.

marks.label: A property
marks.text: One row per property in the package.

marks.label: Its basis
marks.text: The NOI this property counts with. Safe and Aggressive are greyed (“approve it first”) until its underwriting is approved.

marks.label: NOI
marks.text: Its NOI on the basis picked.

marks.label: + ticked pushes
marks.text: What its ticked pushes add.

marks.label: From
marks.text: Where the figure comes from: the T12 and its months, or the approved underwriting and when it was approved.

marks.label: Total
marks.text: The NOI the package is sized on: every property’s NOI, its pushes and your levers.

views.title: Each property’s basis
views.text: Villages of Whitewater switched to its Aggressive underwriting; Queens Gate and The Mews stay on their in-place T12. The total and everything below follow, and each pick is kept with this refinance.

marks.label: Aggressive underwriting
marks.text: Picked for this property only.

marks.label: Its NOI
marks.text: Now its approved Aggressive figure.

marks.label: Total
marks.text: Worked out again.

views.title: Each property’s pushes
views.text: What to push lists each property’s pushes under its name, ticked one by one; a push counts its effect on the basis picked for its property.

marks.label: Villages of Whitewater · on the Aggressive underwriting
marks.text: Its pushes, counted on the basis picked for it.

marks.label: A push ticked
marks.text: Its effect on Aggressive is added to the package’s NOI.

marks.label: Added to the NOI
marks.text: Everything ticked, every property together.

marks.label: Queens Gate Apartments
marks.text: No pushes yet: approve its underwriting in Underwriting first, then What to push lists them.

marks.label: The amount to cover
marks.text: For the whole package.

views.title: The package’s verdict
views.text: “These 3 properties support …”: the verdict and everything after it work exactly as for one loan. **Save as a loan** puts one new loan on all of them and pays off every loan on them.

marks.label: The answer
marks.text: For the whole package.

marks.label: Which properties
marks.text: The properties and the number of loans paid off.

marks.label: You owe (payoff)
marks.text: Every loan on them, added up.

marks.label: Properties support
marks.text: The biggest single loan the properties support together.

marks.label: Today’s loan rate
marks.text: The loans’ rate together, weighted by what is owed.

marks.label: Proposed loan rate
marks.text: The one new loan’s rate.

marks.label: When, and the pay-down
marks.text: What ends first, and the pay-down a new loan needs.

marks.label: Proposed rate
marks.text: The one new loan’s rate type, index and spread.

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: The one new loan.

marks.label: Can you?
marks.text: For all of them together.

marks.label: How “supports $X” is worked out
marks.text: The package’s NOI (every property on its own basis, with its pushes), the rate, the payment, the value and the limits.

marks.label: Bottom line
marks.text: What to do for the package.

views.title: A property with no T12
views.text: Here Queens Gate Apartments and Avalon Norwalk, which has no T12. Counting it as $0, or on a typed NOI, would misstate what the package supports, so nothing is sized until its T12 is uploaded.

marks.label: No T12 yet
marks.text: The package can’t be sized yet.

marks.label: Which property
marks.text: The property with no T12; the others are fine.

marks.label: Upload Avalon Norwalk’s T12 in Underwriting
marks.text: Opens Underwriting on that property, ready for its T12. Come back to the package afterwards.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Back to the Portfolio tab.

pages.title: Save the refinance as a loan
pages.description: Make the proposed loan a loan in your book, and mark today’s loan paid off.
pages.intro: When the answer is **Refinance**, **Your decision** or a pay-down, and the proposed loan matches your lender’s terms, save it. The new loan joins your book, and today’s loan is marked Paid off (refinanced) and leaves every total.
before: A proposed loan on the refinance — see [Set the proposed loan’s rate and amount](set-the-proposed-loan).

steps.text: Open the loan’s refinance and check the proposed loan: its rate, its amount and its terms. Here The Mews at Princeton, with the lender’s spread typed as 0 (made-up).
Click **Save as a loan** at the top. With a pay-down it reads **Save as a loan — pay in $X**; with **Your decision**, **Save as a loan — Refinance now**.

marks.label: Save as a loan
marks.text: Shown only when there is a loan to propose.

steps.text: Read **Save the refinance?**: the new loan, the loan it pays off, and any cash you pay in.

marks.label: Save the refinance?
marks.text: It asks first.

marks.label: What happens
marks.text: The new loan, the old loan(s) paid off, and any cash paid in.

marks.label: Save the refinance
marks.text: Does it.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing changes.

steps.text: Click **Save the refinance**. The new loan is added with today’s date and opens on its own page. Today’s loan becomes Paid off (refinanced) and leaves every total; a pay-down is recorded on the new loan.

callouts.text: For a package, the one new loan secures every property in it, and every loan on them is paid off.

steps.text: On the **Portfolio** tab, scroll down to **Removed & paid-off loans**. Today’s loan is listed there as **Paid off (refinanced)**.

marks.label: Removed & paid-off loans
marks.text: Loans out of every total, tile and the calendar.

marks.label: Today’s loan
marks.text: Paid off (refinanced), with the date.

marks.label: Restore
marks.text: Brings it back into every total.

steps.text: To go back on the refinance, click **Restore** on today’s loan and remove the new loan. See [Bring back a removed loan or property](bring-back-removed) and [Remove a loan](remove-a-loan).

next.text: See the property’s coverage with the new loan.
